title: Surge-triggered output drift and kernel guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a transient capacity surge on 2026-02-28 we observed a reproducible divergence in model outputs (Re-ranker-v3) correlated with a scheduler decision to probe a quantized kernel variant. The divergence was subtle (semantic rerank ordering changes) but caused a ~12% drop in a key downstream metric for one major customer and tripped evaluation regression alerts. This ticket captures the investigation summary, root cause hypothesis, and concrete remediation and guardrail work to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC: traffic surge begins (spike in parallel short-chat requests).
2026-02-28 03:13 UTC: scheduler increases probe_window and initiates kernel candidate probing.
2026-02-28 03:14 UTC: a subset of inference workers switch to experimental quantized kernel QK-v2 under probe.
2026-02-28 03:15-03:40 UTC: downstream reranking metric anomaly detected; eval alert fires at 03:22 UTC.
2026-02-28 03:45 UTC: on-call rolls back probing policy and drains QK-v2 from production. Metrics begin to recover by 04:10 UTC.
2026-02-28 05:00 UTC: initial incident triage; sample traces and outputs collected.
impact_summary: Output ordering for reranking tasks diverged when the quantized kernel handled ~18% of requests during the probe window. This led to a 12% relative regression in the customer's rerank precision@3 and triggered a support escalation. Latency remained within SLOs but unit-quality regressions were unacceptable for production traffic.
reproduction_steps: Checkout runtime commit tag: runtime-1.22-candidate with scheduler-probe-heuristic enabled.
Deploy a canary fleet and configure workload generator to replay the original traffic spike pattern (short parallel chat + rerank requests).
Enable kernel probing for QK-v2 with identical probe_window and probing_rate used during incident (see config snapshot at /links/config-snapshot).
Collect model outputs and compare rerank orderings against a baseline that routes exclusively to the reference kernel RK-v1.
Run the same experiment with KV cache warmed vs cold to reproduce cache-interaction differences.
root_cause_summary: Multiple factors combined: (1) the scheduler's aggressive probe amplification under high concurrency allowed QK-v2 to receive real traffic, (2) QK-v2 implemented a deterministic numeric path that differed in floating-point accumulation order causing rare token-level tie-break changes for rerank scoring, and (3) KV cache eviction timing during high parallelism exposed ordering differences (cold vs warm reads). We underestimated the sensitivity of re-ranking models to tiny numeric differences when selecting alternate kernels during probes.
action_items: (Owner: Priya Nair) Short-term: revert probe amplification override and add a kill-switch in scheduler-config to block kernel probing during high variance capacity events. Target: 2026-03-05.

(Owner: Tomás García) Medium-term: implement deterministic numeric parity tests between kernel candidates using the rerank evaluation suite (microbench + on-the-fly diff tooling). Add to CI gate for kernel onboarding. Target: 2026-03-18.
(Owner: Wei Chen) Medium-term: add KV-cache state fuzz tests covering cold/warm eviction timing to surface ordering-sensitive behaviors. Target: 2026-03-18.

(Owner: SRE Team) Short-term: create a runbook and automation to detect probe-related quality divergence (alert on small but consistent rerank order flips) and automatically restrict probing. Target: 2026-03-10.
(Owner: Product) Long-term: define acceptable bit-level or ranking-tolerance thresholds for kernel substitutions per model class and bake into rollout policies. Target: 2026-04-01.
(Owner: QA) Short-term: add a smoke canary that replays a curated prompt set (sensitive to rerank ordering) during probe windows and fails probe if divergence > threshold. Target: 2026-03-12.
(Owner: Security) Review: confirm no customer data exposure in diagnostic dumps. Target: 2026-03-07.
followups: Schedule cross-team warroom to validate kernel parity harness design (runtime, research, qa) — week of 2026-03-08.
Audit all active kernel candidates and tag those allowed for probing in production with an explicit parity scorecard. Owner: Runtime Onboarding Squad. Due: 2026-03-25.
Add a gating checklist to Dedicated and Private deploy playbooks to disallow probing by default in customer-isolated fleets. Owner: Private Deployments Team. Due: 2026-03-30.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Stricter probe restrictions will slow the pace of kernel onboarding and may delay performance gains from new kernels.
Adding parity gates increases CI runtime and maintenance burden but reduces customer-visible regressions.
Automated runbook actions need careful threshold tuning to avoid over-correcting for benign variance.
communications: Customer notification sent 2026-03-03 with incident summary and mitigation steps. (Support ticket #SUP-11022)
Internal posting to #runtime-ops with links to artifacts and owner assignments on 2026-03-04.
Postmortem write-up scheduled for 2026-03-14 in Confluence.
notes: Empirical observation: not all model families are equally sensitive — rerankers and tight-scoring classifiers are highest risk.
Consider a policy: allow probing for generative-only models with tolerance but require parity tests for deterministic scoring models.
Track the false-positive rate of the new smoke canary over the first 30 days and iterate thresholds.
